newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt share prices continue downtrend.
newsitem.headline: Egypt share prices continue downtrend.

text.p: Shares of the housing sector were the most stable in a declining Cairo market as share prices continued their downtrend on Sunday.
The all-share index shed 6.32 points to end at 368.08 in 42.2 million pounds ($12.4 million) worth of turnover, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said.
"The downtrend continued, but the housing sector was stable," Mohammed Abdullah, Intercapital managing director, told Reuters.

Heliopolis Housing and Development was the second most active share with stock worth 4.41 million pounds traded. The share ended 6.99 pounds higher at 415. But during most of the session it was being dealt at 408 pounds.
"This price should attract buying," said Mohamed Magdi of EFG/Hermes.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement was the most active share and added a tiny 0.04 to close at 94.10 pounds, when equity worth 4.46 million pounds were traded.
Abdullah said mills were no longer attractive because the private sector would soon compete with state-run mills.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills fell 3.30 pounds to close at 85.71 pounds after 2.88 million pounds worth of trade.

"The shares will be registered at the book-keeping company on May 24. As a big number of shares were recently sold in unofficial transactions outside the bourse, those holding share want to get rid of them, otherwise they will lose their money," Magdi said.
Commercial International Bank (CIB) closed down at 73.26 pounds, losing 3.85 pounds. "The dividend, at 2.00 pounds a share, is not attractive as a yield," Magdi said.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 529.3 points from 544.78 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 265.42 from 268.25.
Out of the 79 shares traded, only nine ended up, 40 fell and 30 were unchanged
